# Prompt-format mirroring and structural priming in output — concept pack (small)

> Source-anchored research for Prompt-format mirroring and structural priming in output. Run status: COMPLETED.

<!-- generated by llms-concept-abstractor v1.4.1 · generated 2026-09-23 · budgeted to ≈8000 tokens; the full catalogue is llms-full.txt -->

## How it works

- [statement] Language models show structural priming: they reuse recently seen syntactic structures, including when prime and target share no lexical overlap, indicating abstract structural representations. (high confidence) — https://aclanthology.org/2022.tacl-1.60.pdf · keywords: Prompt-format mirroring and structural priming in output · also: https://arxiv.org/abs/2310.11324

## Comparisons and alternatives

- [statement] Practical mitigation for instruction files: write the instruction file in the plain style wanted in the output (prose, little markdown) and state the desired format positively, rather than only listing prohibitions. (low confidence) — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/prompt-engineering/claude-prompting-best-practices

## Facts and statements

- [statement] Anthropic's prompting guide says the formatting style of a prompt may influence Claude's response style, and that removing markdown from the prompt can reduce the volume of markdown in the output. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-09-23) — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/prompt-engineering/claude-prompting-best-practices · keywords: Prompt-format mirroring and structural priming in output · also: https://arxiv.org/abs/2310.11324
- [statement] Prompt format alone can change measured performance a lot: up to 76 accuracy points on LLaMA-2-13B in few-shot settings, persisting with larger models, more shots, or instruction tuning; format performance correlates only weakly across models. (high confidence) — https://arxiv.org/abs/2310.11324 · keywords: Prompt-format mirroring and structural priming in output · also: https://arxiv.org/html/2411.10541v1
- [statement] Format sensitivity falls with model strength: GPT-4 variants varied less across plain text, markdown, JSON and YAML than GPT-3.5-turbo, and no single format is best across models. (medium confidence) — https://arxiv.org/html/2411.10541v1 · keywords: Prompt-format mirroring and structural priming in output · also: https://arxiv.org/abs/2310.11324
- [statement] A 2026 study (9,649 experiments, 11 models, YAML/markdown/JSON/TOON context) found no significant aggregate accuracy effect of context format (p=0.484), though individual models, mostly open-source, showed format-specific differences. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-02-01) — https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.05447
